lines.text: The camera can see a tag and work out where the robot is. Now the robot has to listen.
Install the Limelight library from its vendor file. The address is pinned to the WPILib alpha, so copy it exactly.
There are two ways to solve a pose. One works out the heading from the tags. The other borrows the robot's own heading, and that's the one to trust with a single tag.
So every loop, the robot sends its heading to the camera first.
The camera and the robot run on different clocks. Reading the frame queue takes exactly the frames that arrived, no more and no fewer.
Some sightings get thrown out: anything the library flags, and anything more than four meters away.
The rest get weighed. Far away, the error circle grows. A second tag shrinks it to a quarter.
Each picture was taken a moment ago. The estimator rewinds to that moment, folds the sighting in, and replays forward to now.
Try it. Cover the camera, push the robot, then uncover it.
It doesn't jump. The estimate walks back over about a second, and faster when the sighting is good.
Blend the camera into the pose. Don't replace the pose with the camera.
